statement: A ladder has 9 rungs. Ben stands on the middle rung. Then he climbs up 2 rungs. How many rungs are below him now?

choices.misconception: I counted only the rungs he climbed past between where he started and where he stopped.
I counted the rungs above him instead of the rungs below him.
I counted the rungs below the middle rung and forgot that he climbed up 2.
I thought the middle rung of 9 rungs was rung 4, so Ben climbed to rung 6 and had 5 rungs below him.

hints: Draw the ladder and number the rungs from the bottom.
Draw 9 rungs. The middle rung has the same number of rungs above it as below it. Mark it, move up 2 rungs, then count what is underneath.
The middle rung has 4 rungs below it and 4 above it. After climbing, Ben has 2 more rungs below him than before.

solutions.reliable: Number the rungs 1 to 9 from the bottom. The middle rung is rung 5, with 4 rungs below it and 4 above it. Ben climbs up 2 rungs to rung 7. The rungs below him are rungs 1 to 6, so there are 6. The idea to keep: a quick drawing with numbers turns a muddle of words into something you can count.
solutions.elegant: Climbing up 2 rungs puts 2 more rungs under Ben. He started with 4 below him, so now there are 4 + 2 = 6. The idea to keep: think about what changes, not just where you end up.

whyOnTest: Drawing the diagram: a sketch of the ladder makes the middle rung and the climb easy to count, while doing it in your head invites off-by-one slips.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
